jurisdiction.name: Liechtenstein
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Liechtenstein has no AI-specific law yet: the EU AI Act still awaits incorporation into the EEA Agreement and a national implementing act. Its AI governance rests on the government's 2026 AI Strategy for the national administration, the 2018 Data Protection Act, which regulates automated individual decisions and profiling, and the data protection authority's guidance on AI, chatbots and the risks of the DeepSeek service. Liechtenstein is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
lead_institutions: Government of the Principality of Liechtenstein
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official law database, the government's and the data protection authority's websites; a run cut off by a usage limit was resumed and its downloads re-verified against the live official sources. The national administration portal (llv.li) and the financial market authority's site could not be accessed, so the education office's AI teaching guideline and the government's May 2026 reply to Parliament on AI are tracked as leads, together with the EEA incorporation of the AI Act.

instruments.english_title: AI Strategy of the Liechtenstein National Administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Principality of Liechtenstein (prepared by the Task Force KI under the Ministry for General Government Affairs and Finance)
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Government at its meeting of 14 April 2026 and published with the full text and a short version on 21 April 2026 (Government media release; document version 1.0, last amended 9 April 2026). It has no fixed validity period; a fundamental revision is due by 2030 at the latest. The strategy notes that the EU AI Act still awaits incorporation into the EEA Agreement and that Liechtenstein's AI Act authorities have not yet been designated (to be set out in an implementing act).
instruments.summary: Strategy adopted by the Government for the whole Liechtenstein National Administration (LLV), setting a vision, mission and four principles (responsible, human-centred, transparent, efficient and innovative) for using AI. It sets goals and measures in four fields of action (people, organisation, governance, infrastructure), including AI training, an organisational concept with defined roles, a release and compliance process for AI tools, a uniform risk assessment and pre-classification of AI uses against the EU AI Act risk categories, an internal AI use inventory and controlled testing environments. It replaces the 2023 basic paper on AI use with a new internal 'KI-Merkblatt' and anchors the work in the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe AI Convention, which Liechtenstein signed in February 2025.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI strategy of the Liechtenstein government; governs AI use across the national administration and prepares AI Act implementation.

instruments.current_status: Published in the Landesgesetzblatt, LGBl. 2018 Nr. 272, issued 7 December 2018; in force on 1 January 2019 under art. 91 (in force on 1 January 2019 subject to the referendum period expiring unused). Consolidated version in force from 1 April 2026 on gesetze.li.
instruments.summary: Liechtenstein's general data protection law, which implements the GDPR (applicable via the EEA) and transposes the Law Enforcement Directive (EU) 2016/680, and applies to processing by public bodies and to automated processing by private bodies. Art. 37 restricts the GDPR art. 22 right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, including profiling, permitting solely automated decisions (beyond the GDPR art. 22(2)(a) and (c) exceptions) in insurance-contract benefits, due-diligence risk assessment under the Due Diligence Act and credit business, subject to safeguards, and the Act sets the powers of the Data Protection Authority (Datenschutzstelle). It is the main national law governing the use of personal data to train and run AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law governing automated decision-making, profiling and personal-data processing by AI systems.

instruments.current_status: Published on the Authority's 'Themen A-Z' pages; announced in its news item of 27 October 2023. Page reachable on 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Guidance from the Datenschutzstelle on the data protection requirements for operating chatbots, including generative AI chatbots such as ChatGPT. It requires controllers to identify the correct GDPR legal basis (art. 6(1), and art. 9(2) for special-category data), inform users transparently about all processing, and consider cookies, storage periods, sensitive data and reuse of chatbot data by processors for their own purposes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator guidance on deploying AI-based chatbots in compliance with the GDPR.

instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence (data protection information and guidance)
instruments.current_status: Published on the Authority's 'Themen A-Z' pages; announced in its news item of 9 May 2023. Page reachable on 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Information article by the Datenschutzstelle explaining AI and generative AI systems (e.g. ChatGPT), their opportunities and risks, and how they interact with data protection law. It states that a fully data-protection-compliant, risk-free use of public cloud-based generative AI with personal data is not yet possible and advises users, as an interim rule, not to enter personal data or other sensitive data (professional or business secrets) into such systems, especially large language models.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator's interim guidance on personal data in generative AI tools.

instruments.official_title: Wichtiger Hinweis: Risiken bei der Nutzung von DeepSeek
instruments.english_title: Important notice: risks of using DeepSeek
instruments.current_status: News notice dated 13.02.2025 on the Authority's website; reachable on 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Notice from the Datenschutzstelle warning that the generative AI model DeepSeek R1 poses serious data protection risks because prompts may be recorded and processed without adequate safeguards, processing takes place in China and the provider has no EU/EEA representative. It recommends not installing the DeepSeek model in any IT environment, never entering personal or confidential data in its online interface, and preferring AI tools that comply with the GDPR and the AI Act.
